hints: The definition specifies what a field line represents at a point, rather than only its drawn shape.
State the direction of force or motion for a free positive test charge.
walkthrough: A field line represents the direction of the electric force at each point in an electric field.
The conventional test charge is positive, so the line gives the direction in which a free positive charge would move.
Thus, a field line is a line whose direction shows the force on a positive test charge.

ai_rubric.observable: States that a field line gives the path or direction in which a free positive charge moves, or equivalently the direction of force on it.

hints: Field-line density represents field strength: compare the spacing of neighbouring lines in the two regions.
Region Y has the greater field strength.
walkthrough: A stronger electric field is represented by a greater density of field lines.
Since the field strength in Y is greater than in X, the lines in Y are closer together.
Equivalently, the field lines in X are further apart than those in Y.

ai_rubric.observable: States that field lines are closer together in Y, or equivalently further apart in X.

hints: Combine F = ma with the electric-force magnitude F = Eq, so acceleration in the same field is proportional to |q| / m.
For an α-particle, use charge magnitude 2e and mass 4u before forming the ratio P to α.
walkthrough: Equating the electric force to the resultant force gives ma = E|q|, so a = E|q| / m.
In the same field, the E factor cancels in the ratio: aₚ / aᵅ = (e / 0.15u) / (2e / 4u).
Therefore aₚ / aᵅ = (1 / 0.15) × (4 / 2) = 13.3..., so the ratio is 13.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses a = E|q| / m, or combines F = E|q| with F = ma.
Forms the acceleration ratio as (1e / 0.15u) × (4u / 2e), or an algebraically equivalent expression.

hints: A down quark has charge −e / 3; subtract this from the particle's total charge of −e.
Identify a quark or antiquark flavour with the remaining charge of −2e / 3.
walkthrough: The down quark contributes a charge of −e / 3.
The other constituent must therefore have charge −e − (−e / 3) = −2e / 3.
An anti-up quark has charge −2e / 3, so anti-up is a possible answer. Anti-charm or anti-top would also have this charge.

ai_rubric.observable: States that a down quark has charge −e / 3.
Identifies anti-up as a possible flavour; anti-charm or anti-top are also valid.
